terms.comment: Augustus’ seven cohorts of the watch, Rome’s night police and fire brigade (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for the police. Their commander, the praefectus vigilum, is his chief of police (p. 194).

terms.gloss: guardians of public safety: police officers
evidence: Levi–Bini p. 49: cūrātōrēs pūblicae disciplīnae (or sēcūritātis)
terms.comment: Egger’s name for a police officer, in the plural.

terms.gloss: chief of police (the prefect of the watch)

phrases.english: Did you call the police? — I did.

phrases.latin: vigilēs, quī custōdiēbant vīcīnam regiōnem, ratī ārdēre Trimalchiōnis domum, effrēgērunt jānuam subitō
phrases.english: the watch, who were guarding the neighbourhood, thought Trimalchio’s house was on fire and suddenly broke the door down

sources: Lewis & Short: vigil · Lewis & Short: publicus · Lewis & Short: securitas · Lewis & Short: custos
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 193, 194, 290.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. policeman.
Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 49, s.v. polizia.
